notices.html: Book ahead for Bellemont Farm's Sunflower Festival: advance online tickets ($19 adult, $12 kids) are cheaper than at the door ($25, $15), and the festival runs weekends through September 13 if this one's booked up.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: blackberries and cut-your-own flowers are still pick-your-own at Terhune, but there's no peach or apple picking this year after the spring freeze, so save the orchard trip for later in fall. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm what's ripe before you go.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: no fresh dated update is posted for this small, family-run farm, but late August typically brings peaches, apples, nectarines, pears and cantaloupe for pick-your-own. Call 609-448-0629 to confirm the day's picking before you head over.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: blackberries are still pick-your-own at the Monmouth Junction fields, open daily 10 to 5, with a $3 per person field admission. Apples aren't ready and the fall festival with the corn maze doesn't open until mid-September. Call 732-329-8656 to confirm what's ready to pick.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: Emery's u-pick blueberry season has wrapped for the year, though fresh and frozen berries are still sold in the farm market. No update was found on cut-your-own sunflowers, so call 609-758-8514 to check before a special trip.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: the spring freeze wiped out this year's sour cherry, peach, nectarine and apple crops, so pick-your-own fruit isn't available at Battleview. The country store and bakery are still open for cider donuts. Call 732-462-0756 to confirm hours before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: Johnson's still has peaches to pick along with tomatoes, zucchini and other late-summer vegetables, and the Sunflower Celebration hayride to the flower fields runs Thursday through Sunday, 4:30 to 6:30pm, stems $1.50 each. Call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to confirm before you drive over.
